title: Motion-compensated memory pages: shifted reference plus residual
idea: Borrowing H.264 P-frame motion compensation: a CXL memory controller finds, for each cold 4 KB page, a reference page and a byte-offset 'motion vector' (pages that match after a shift, e.g. realigned structs or shifted buffers) and stores only the vector plus an entropy-coded residual; reads reconstruct in a short pipeline from a hot reference-page cache.
why: Catches near-duplicates that exact dedup and per-line compression miss (VM images, JVM heaps, checkpoint shards); claims 1.5-3x extra capacity on cold tiers, lowering cost per usable bit.

title: JPEG for the KV cache: DCT along the token axis
idea: Treat each attention head's K and V as an image (tokens x channels), apply a block DCT along the token axis where neighbouring tokens correlate, and quantize with per-head learned quantization tables like JPEG luminance tables; the attention kernel inverse-transforms blocks in SRAM.
why: KV cache dominates long-context inference memory; transform coding before quantization claims 4-8x smaller KV at <1% quality loss vs ~2-4x for plain quantization.

title: Floyd-Steinberg dithering for 2-bit KV and activation storage
idea: Borrow error-diffusion halftoning from printing: when quantizing KV vectors to 2 bits, push each token's quantization error into the next token's pre-quantization value so errors cancel in the attention-weighted sum instead of accumulating as bias.
why: Makes ultra-low-bit storage (2 vs 16 bits) usable because attention sums many tokens and diffused error averages out; ~8x KV capacity.

title: Foveated KV cache: precision decays with attention distance
idea: Like VR foveated rendering, keep full precision only where attention 'gazes' (recent tokens and tokens with high cumulative attention mass) and step other tokens down 16->8->4->2 bits as their attention mass fades, using a background demotion engine that re-encodes in place.
why: Most tokens are peripheral; averages 3-4 bits/value instead of 16, a 4-5x KV memory reduction with full quality where it matters.

title: MP3 bit reservoir: fixed compressed slots with borrowed bits
idea: MP3 frames borrow unused bits from a shared reservoir to hold a constant bitrate; likewise every compressed page gets a fixed 2 KB slot (address = index x 2 KB, no translation table) and pages that overflow borrow 256 B chunks from a per-region reservoir located via a tiny overflow bitmap.
why: Variable-size memory compression needs translation tables and fragmentation handling that add latency; fixed slots plus a reservoir keep O(1) addressing while capturing ~1.8-2x capacity.

title: Airline overbooking for RAM: overcommit by measured no-show rate
idea: Hypervisors record, per application class, the fraction of allocated memory never touched ('no-shows') and overbook physical DRAM by that rate, with a pre-agreed bump protocol (compress, then demote to CXL flash) for rare oversubscription and a yield-managed premium for guaranteed seats.
why: Cloud VMs often touch only 40-60% of allocated RAM; statistical overbooking could cut provisioned DRAM per VM 25-40%.

title: Memory futures market inside the cluster scheduler
idea: Borrow commodity futures: jobs buy forward contracts for GB-hours at submission, the scheduler clears the market every minute, and spot-price spikes automatically switch jobs into pre-registered compressed or recompute modes or let them sell capacity back.
why: Price signals reveal which jobs can shrink cheaply; claims 15-25% lower peak DRAM provisioning in shared AI clusters by flattening demand.

title: Pointer dehydration: hardware shrinks 64-bit pointers on eviction
idea: Like dehydrating food for storage, the memory controller detects 64-bit pointers in evicted cache lines (high bits match a region-base register) and stores them as 32-bit region offsets, packing a 64 B line into 32-40 B; rehydration on fill is a single add.
why: Pointer-heavy workloads (graphs, JVM, Python, databases) are 30-50% pointers; transparent 1.3-1.6x capacity without software changes.

title: RAID for RAM: erasure-coded stripes replace triple-copy replicas
idea: Distributed in-memory stores (Redis replicas, parameter servers, failover KV-cache copies) keep 2-3 full copies; instead stripe data with Reed-Solomon (e.g. 8+2) across nodes' DRAM over RDMA/CXL and reconstruct on node loss as RAID-6 does for disks.
why: Cuts redundancy overhead from 200% to 25%, ~2.4x less DRAM for fault-tolerant in-memory tiers.

title: Bullwhip damping: cache each block in exactly one stack layer
idea: Like supply chains where every tier hoards safety stock, the app cache, runtime, OS page cache, hypervisor and storage controller each cache the same block; a cross-layer exclusive-caching protocol passes block ownership tokens on eviction so each block lives in exactly one layer.
why: Duplicate caching wastes 20-40% of server DRAM in database and AI data-loading stacks.

title: Stock reduction: simmer near-duplicate tokens into weighted KV entries
idea: As a chef reduces stock to concentrate flavour, a background pass merges runs of KV entries whose keys are near-duplicates into one centroid entry carrying a count that adds log(count) to its attention logit, preserving attention mass.
why: Long contexts are full of repetitive tokens; 2-5x fewer stored KV entries for documents and code with attention mass conserved on merged clusters.

title: Epigenetic masks: tenant model variants as methylation over shared base
idea: Like methylation silencing genes without changing DNA, each customer fine-tune is stored as a sparse binary mask plus per-row scales over one shared base model, applied on the fly inside the matmul kernel instead of keeping a full copy.
why: Serving 1,000 variants needs one base plus ~1/16-size masks each instead of 1,000 copies; order-of-magnitude weight-memory savings in multi-tenant serving.

title: Capsule wardrobe weights: one global codebook for every layer
idea: A capsule wardrobe mixes a few garments into many outfits; store one model-wide codebook of 64K 8-dim weight vectors in on-chip SRAM and represent every layer as 16-bit indices into it (2 bits/weight), trained with codebook-aware fine-tuning.
why: 2 bits/weight with a shared on-chip codebook avoids per-layer codebook overhead; ~8x smaller weights in DRAM vs FP16.

title: CDMA embedding tables: superposed rows with orthogonal spreading codes
idea: Like CDMA letting many phones share one channel, rarely accessed embedding rows of different IDs are summed into the same physical row after multiplying by pseudo-random +/-1 codes; a lookup multiplies by the ID's code to despread, leaving the others as low-level noise.
why: Recommender embedding tables are TB-scale with a long tail; 4-16x compression of tail rows with graceful noise instead of hard hash collisions.

title: Map-tile mipmaps: multi-resolution embeddings split across DRAM and flash
idea: Like web maps loading coarse tiles before fine ones, store a 4-bit coarse version of each embedding or retrieval vector in DRAM and its residual refinement levels on flash; the model uses the coarse level by default and fetches residuals only when a confidence check fails.
why: Most lookups are satisfied at the coarse level; ~4x less DRAM for large embedding and retrieval indexes with flash serving <10% of reads.

title: Git-style Merkle heap: forked agent sessions share unchanged memory
idea: Represent a process's heap and KV state as a content-addressed Merkle tree of 4 KB chunks with hardware-assisted hashing; forking an agent (tree search, best-of-N, multi-agent branches) copies only the root and the diverging chunks, like git branches.
why: Agentic workloads fork state constantly; N branches cost ~1x plus deltas instead of Nx, a 5-20x DRAM saving for tree-search inference.

title: Sushi conveyor: weights circulate a ring, each chip grabs its plate
idea: Model layers circulate continuously on an optical/SerDes ring of accelerators like plates on a kaiten-sushi belt; each chip computes on the layer passing it and holds only a 2-3 layer window locally instead of a full or gathered copy.
why: Per-chip weight memory drops by roughly the ring size while ring bandwidth, not HBM capacity, sets throughput; attacks the HBM capacity tax.

title: Second-life DRAM: retired DDR4 reborn in CXL cold tiers
idea: Like EV batteries repurposed for grid storage, harvest DDR4 DIMMs from decommissioned servers, bin them with a test robot, and mount them in CXL expansion boxes acting as a compressed cold tier behind new DDR5.
why: Avoids buying new bits for the coldest 30-50% of memory; supply relief at near-zero marginal cost and zero new wafers.

title: Shared parking for memory: co-locate day and night workloads
idea: Like office parking reused by residents at night, pair anti-correlated workloads (daytime inference, night batch training/ETL) on one DRAM pool and swap working sets via fast NVMe snapshots at shift change, sizing DRAM to the peak of the sum rather than the sum of peaks.
why: Peak-of-sum vs sum-of-peaks can save 30-45% of fleet DRAM where diurnal patterns are strong.

title: Net metering for RAM: credits for ballooning memory back
idea: Like rooftop-solar owners selling surplus to the grid, cloud tenants run a balloon agent that hands unused RAM back to the provider in real time and earns per-GB-minute credits at the current spot price, redeemable when they need to grow.
why: Turns idle tenant DRAM (often 30%+) into reusable supply through incentive design rather than new silicon.

title: Drop-shipping data: zero-inventory host memory for AI servers
idea: Like retailers that hold no stock and let suppliers ship direct, enforce a single-copy I/O path: storage DMAs straight into accelerator memory, page-cache and pinned bounce-buffer copies are eliminated, and the host keeps only metadata.
why: AI servers ship with 1-2 TB of host DRAM largely used as staging copies; could cut host DRAM 50-70% per node.

title: Kanban cards for layer streaming from SSD to GPU
idea: Toyota-style kanban: a hardware credit counter between the GPU and an NVMe controller releases the next layer's weights or KV pages only when a consumer slot frees, so DRAM/HBM holds exactly pipeline-depth (2-3 layers) of inventory, never the whole model.
why: Runs models 5-10x larger than HBM at near-full batch throughput; substitutes cheap flash bandwidth for DRAM capacity.

title: Table-side hot pot: attention cooked inside the memory module
idea: Like hot pot where diners cook at the table instead of the kitchen, put decode-attention units inside commodity LPDDR CXL modules so the KV cache never leaves them; the GPU sends the query vector and receives the attention output.
why: Moves the largest inference memory consumer out of scarce HBM (~3x wafer per bit) into commodity DRAM and cuts decode data-movement energy ~5-10x.

title: Blast chiller: compress lines at LLC eviction straight into NV log
idea: Like blast chillers freezing food before ice crystals form, a 'chiller' engine at the last-level cache compresses evicted lines predicted cold and appends them directly to a persistent NAND/MRAM log on CXL, bypassing DRAM; reads of chilled lines return through a small decompress buffer.
why: Cold data never occupies DRAM even briefly and is durable on arrival; claims a 2-3x smaller DRAM tier with persistence included.

title: Sleep consolidation: idle gaps distil sessions into persistent memory tokens
idea: Like the hippocampus replaying the day into cortex during sleep, while a chat or agent session is idle the server compresses its KV cache into ~64 learned memory tokens written to persistent flash and frees the DRAM; the session resumes by loading those tokens.
why: Idle sessions hold 60-90% of KV memory in chat serving; compact persistent summaries free most of it and survive power loss.

title: Vinyl pressing: frozen model weights stamped into via-programmed ROM
idea: Like pressing millions of records from one master, burn a released model's weights into via- or metal-programmed ROM chiplets (mature node, one custom mask, no EUV) bonded beside the accelerator; weights are inherently non-volatile and DRAM holds only KV and small LoRA patches.
why: ROM needs no capacitor or refresh and is several times denser than DRAM at mature nodes; removes weights from DRAM entirely and is U.S.-manufacturable on existing fabs.

title: Card catalog: tiny learned index in DRAM, records in NV
idea: Like a library card catalog pointing into the stacks, keep a piecewise-linear learned index of a few MB in DRAM that predicts the exact NV page holding any key, so each lookup costs one byte-addressable NV read and records never need DRAM residency.
why: Key-value index memory shrinks 10-100x vs DRAM B-trees and data stays durable on CXL-NAND or MRAM.

title: Seed bank weights: PRNG seeds plus low-rank corrections in NV
idea: Like a seed vault storing seeds instead of forests, store each weight block as a 32-bit PRNG seed selecting a random basis, a few coefficients and a low-rank residual in on-package NV; a hardware LFSR regrows the block in SRAM at compute time.
why: ~3-4 bits per weight-equivalent, zero DRAM for weights, native persistence; trades cheap logic for scarce memory.

title: Sourdough starter: persist tokens, regrow KV on demand
idea: Keep only the starter: persist each session's token IDs (2-4 bytes per token) to flash and drop its KV cache (100 KB+ per token on large models) under pressure; a cost model chooses between regrowing KV by prefill on idle compute and fetching a stored copy.
why: Persistent state shrinks ~10^4-10^5x per token; exploits compute being more abundant than memory.

title: Flight recorder: MRAM intent journal makes DRAM a crash-safe cache
idea: Like an aircraft black box logging only essential parameters, a small MRAM ring records memory-tier metadata (page-map updates, dirty-line intents, epoch markers) so a flash-backed memory can treat DRAM purely as a volatile cache and rebuild consistent state after power loss.
why: Lets cheap NAND carry capacity with DRAM shrunk to the working set and no NVDIMM batteries; MRAM needed is ~0.1% of capacity.

title: Torpor mode: idle containers hibernate to NV, keeping heartbeat pages
idea: Like animals in torpor keeping only vital functions, idle containers and serverless functions are snapshotted to CXL-attached persistent flash in milliseconds, leaving only profiled heartbeat pages (timers, socket state) in DRAM, with userfaultfd lazy restore on wake.
why: Warm-but-idle instances dominate serverless DRAM; 5-10x more warm instances per GB, and state survives power loss.

title: Back-EMF flush: fan and PSU inertia power the persistence dump
idea: As hard drives use spindle back-EMF to park heads on power loss, harvest the rotational energy of server fans (~10-15 J each) and PSU bulk capacitors through a boost converter to flush a bounded dirty set from DRAM to on-board NAND (~3 J per GB).
why: Makes DRAM-as-cache-over-flash power-safe without batteries or supercaps, so DRAM can shrink to a dirty-bounded cache over cheap persistent flash.

title: Android lifecycle for servers: killable services with saved state bundles
idea: Like Android killing background apps after they save an instance-state bundle, a server framework requires each service to serialize its minimal semantic state (not its heap) to persistent memory on a trim signal, so the OS can kill idle services aggressively and rehydrate them later.
why: Semantic state is often 100-1000x smaller than the heap; reclaims DRAM from idle microservices and makes their state power-safe.

title: Latent image writes: retention-tuned NV programming for short-lived data
idea: Like exposed-but-undeveloped film, data predicted short-lived is written to NV (SLC NAND, MRAM, ReRAM) with weak fast pulses giving days of retention, enough to survive outages, and is 'developed' with full-strength pulses only if it lives long; a lifetime predictor picks the mode.
why: Lets non-volatile media absorb DRAM-tier write traffic with 3-10x less write energy and wear, shrinking the DRAM tier while staying persistent.

title: Player piano: cold MoE experts computed inside 3D NAND
idea: Like a piano roll that plays the instrument directly, store rarely routed mixture-of-experts weights in 3D NAND with string-level analog multiply-accumulate (bitline current summing); the token vector goes to the NAND die and only the expert output returns, while hot experts stay in HBM.
why: MoE models leave 90%+ of parameters idle per token; computing the cold majority inside persistent NAND removes it from DRAM/HBM, ~5-10x less memory per model.

title: Shingled zones for heaps: tenured objects append to zoned NV
idea: Like shingled-magnetic-recording drives writing bands sequentially, a generational garbage collector keeps the nursery in DRAM and promotes survivors by appending them to zoned persistent flash; reclaiming a zone copies live objects forward, matching NAND erase-block physics.
why: The tenured generation is most of a managed heap and rarely written; moves 60-80% of heap bytes from DRAM onto durable media.

title: Holographic recall: attention keys searched in NV analog CAM
idea: Like holographic associative memories returning the stored image closest to a probe, store KV keys in a FeFET/ReRAM analog content-addressable array that computes query-key similarity in place and returns top-k token addresses; only those k values are read from NV value storage.
why: Long-context KV becomes non-volatile and sparsely accessed; KV DRAM need drops 10x+ and attention scan energy falls.

title: Lending library: rack-wide shared read-only NV pages mapped in place
idea: Like a public library replacing private bookshelves, OS images, shared libraries, container layers and model weights live once in a rack-level persistent CXL memory appliance mapped read-only (DAX) into every host, so no host spends DRAM caching its own copy.
why: Removes per-host duplicates of identical read-mostly data (often 10-30% of DRAM) across 32-64 hosts.

title: ER triage at malloc: lifetime-predicted placement into DRAM or NV
idea: Like emergency rooms triaging on arrival, a profiler tags each allocation site with predicted object lifetime and write intensity, and the allocator places long-lived read-mostly objects directly in persistent memory at birth while only short-lived write-hot objects get DRAM.
why: Avoids later migration cost; most bytes are long-lived and read-mostly, so DRAM footprint shrinks 2-3x and long-lived state is durable.

title: Pupation: cold pointer structures metamorphose into succinct NV forms
idea: Like a caterpillar reorganizing into a compact pupa, cold pointer-rich structures (tries, graphs, inverted indexes) are rebuilt into succinct rank/select encodings (Elias-Fano, wavelet trees) stored in byte-addressable NV and queried in place without decompression.
why: Succinct forms approach entropy and are 5-20x smaller than pointer forms; data stays durable and off DRAM.

title: Vehicle-to-grid sessions: clients store their own encrypted state
idea: Like EVs lending their batteries to the grid, user devices persist their own compressed, encrypted, MAC-tagged session state (quantized gist/KV tokens, app session) in local flash and upload it with the next request, so servers hold no DRAM for idle users.
why: Idle-user state is the bulk of serving memory; pushes it onto already-paid-for client flash and sizes server DRAM only to active requests.

title: RFID sweep: in-storage parallel scan replaces DRAM indexes
idea: Like an RFID reader inventorying a whole warehouse in one sweep instead of consulting a ledger, records in NV carry their own tags and computational-storage controllers scan all flash channels in parallel, using per-block Bloom summaries kept in the NV itself, eliminating DRAM-resident indexes.
why: Secondary indexes can rival data size in DRAM; 100+ GB/s internal flash bandwidth makes index-free lookup viable for many queries.

title: Leitner boxes: spaced-repetition promotion from NV into DRAM
idea: Like flashcards moving up Leitner boxes only after recalls at spaced intervals, pages live in persistent memory by default and are promoted one box at a time (NV -> compressed DRAM -> plain DRAM) only after accesses at increasing intervals, filtering one-off scans.
why: Prevents scan pollution from bloating DRAM tiers; keeps DRAM to the truly recurrent working set, ~20-30% smaller for the same hit rate.

title: Ice-storage KV: precompute corpus attention caches off-peak into NV
idea: Like buildings that freeze ice at night to cool by day, compute KV caches for frequently retrieved RAG documents and system prompts off-peak and store them in persistent flash; at query time they are streamed in and position-corrected rather than prefilled and held in DRAM.
why: Removes repeated prefill and replicated DRAM caches of shared documents; 3-5x DRAM saving in RAG serving.

title: Solera optimizer: staggered moment updates live in persistent flash
idea: Like a sherry solera where only a fraction of each barrel is drawn and topped up per cycle, keep Adam's first and second moments in persistent CXL flash and update only a rotating 1/k slice per step (the rest use slightly stale moments), bounding NV write rate and wear while weights stay in HBM.
why: Optimizer state is 2-3x weight size in training; moves it to durable cheap media and doubles as continuous checkpointing.

title: Contact sheets: statistical sketches in DRAM, full records in NV
idea: Like photographers picking from thumbnails before pulling negatives, keep probabilistic sketches (count-min, HyperLogLog, quantile digests) in DRAM and full records in persistent memory; queries that tolerate bounded error are answered from sketches and only exact queries touch NV.
why: Sketches are 100-1000x smaller than raw data; analytics DRAM shrinks drastically while ground truth stays durable.
